summary: A former Mae Ping tobacco-processing estate in San Pa Tong, about 30 km south of Chiang Mai, where preserved curing barns, a museum, cafés and resort sit among mature trees. The architecture and adaptive reuse are the main draw; this is a countryside outing rather than a quick city stop.
whyGo: See tobacco-drying barns from different building periods and learn how the estate has been repurposed.
Combine the heritage visit with northern Thai food, drinks or a quiet garden break.
The conservation project received UNESCO Asia-Pacific’s 2018 award for New Design in Heritage Contexts.
bestFor: Travelers who enjoy a slow café-and-garden visit
Visitors with a car or a planned southern Chiang Mai day trip
skipIf: You have limited time in Chiang Mai and prefer sights within the Old City.
You need a confirmed daily museum schedule, public transport connection or step-free route before setting out.
duration: Allow 2–3 hours on site as a planning estimate for the grounds, museum and a meal; travel time from the city is roughly 45 minutes by car according to the Tourism Authority of Thailand listing.
cost: Admission and museum fees are not clearly published in current sources. Budget separately for transport, food and drinks; confirm any museum charge with the estate before travel.
hours: Current daily opening hours are not verified. A July 2023 local feature described a free museum tour Tuesday–Friday at 4 pm; treat this as historical information and reconfirm directly before planning around it.
bestTime: Visit in daylight to see the barns and shaded grounds. December is generally a comfortable season for an outdoor visit, but check weather and operating hours close to the date.
gettingThere: At 1 Moo 6, Chiang Mai–Hot Road, Ban Klang, San Pa Tong. TAT lists about 45 minutes from Chiang Mai city by car. A private car or driver is the most practical plan; public transit and ride-hail availability for the return trip are uncertain, so arrange transport both ways.
booking: No advance booking requirement for a casual visit was found. Contact Kaomai Lanna at +66 53 481 201 or service@kaomailanna.com to confirm public access, museum arrangements, current hours and restaurant service. Reserve separately if staying overnight.
accessibility: Accessibility details are not published in the sources reviewed. The estate has historic barns and outdoor lanes; ask about steps, uneven paths, accessible toilets and vehicle drop-off before visiting if these matter.
practicalTips: Call ahead: the available tour-time detail is from 2023, while current sources do not give a regular museum schedule.
Plan a return ride before arriving; the estate is outside Chiang Mai’s urban core.
The current TAT profile describes the museum as an AR-supported history experience and lists Café Long Bom and Poo Lien Bistro; check which venues are open on your date.
Pair with nearby San Pa Tong or Doi Inthanon-area stops only after checking drive times and opening schedules.
decemberNotes: For December 2026, no dated seasonal program or special opening notice was found. Expect this to work best as a daytime countryside excursion; confirm hours, museum access, food service and transport shortly before the visit. Peak holiday demand may affect accommodation, so book lodging directly if staying overnight.
uncertainties: Daily public visiting hours, museum admission and whether the Tuesday–Friday 4 pm tour still runs.
